title: Material Alchemy Workshop
description: The user operates a virtual material alchemy workshop where a ShaderBall serves as a calibration reference and a translucent teacup acts as the target object. By adjusting lighting color, intensity, environment rotation, transmission tint, roughness, and metalness through on-screen controls, the user must match the teacup's appearance to a randomly generated target swatch displayed in the corner, validated at each step.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (via importmap from cdn.jsdelivr.net) that implements a Material Alchemy Workshop. Load DiffuseTransmissionTeacup.glb on the right and ShaderBall.glb on the left of the scene, both on a reflective ground plane. Use GLTFLoader and place the camera at position (0, 1.5, 4) looking at the origin. Add an HDR-style environment using PMREMGenerator with a procedurally generated cubemap for reflections. Add one DirectionalLight and one PointLight that orbits slowly. On load, generate a random target appearance defined by 6 parameters: light color (hex), light intensity (0.5-3.0), environment rotation (0-360 degrees), transmission tint color for the teacup, roughness (0-1), and metalness (0-1). Display the target as a colored swatch panel in the top-right corner showing the target tint and a text summary of target values. Create an HTML control panel on the left side with: (1) a color picker for light color, (2) a slider for light intensity, (3) a slider for environment rotation that rotates the environment map, (4) a color picker for teacup transmission tint applied to the teacup material's color property, (5) a slider for roughness applied to the teacup material, (6) a slider for metalness applied to the teacup material. The ShaderBall acts as a live reference showing how the current lighting and environment affect a neutral material. Each parameter change updates the scene in real time. Add a Validate button that checks all 6 parameters against the target within tolerances: colors within delta-E of 15, numeric values within 0.1. Display per-parameter pass/fail indicators. Track interaction steps and show a step counter. Add OrbitControls for camera navigation. Use a dark background with subtle grid on the ground plane. All UI should be styled with semi-transparent dark panels and clean typography.
